desc:
Given an integer array nums and an integer k, return true if there are two different indices i and j such that nums[i] == nums[j] and |i - j| ≤ k. Otherwise return false.

For example, nums = [1, 2, 3, 1] with k = 3 gives true (indices 0 and 3), while nums = [1, 2, 3, 1, 2, 3] with k = 2 gives false: equal values are always three positions apart.
hints: Comparing every pair of indices at distance at most k is correct but can be slow. What do you really need to know about a value you see again?
Only the most recent earlier position of each value matters: if the closest previous equal element is farther than k, every older one is farther still.
Keep a hash map from value to its last index. At index i, if the value is in the map and i - last ≤ k, answer true; then store i as the new last index.
editorial: Walk through the array once while remembering, for every value, the last index where it appeared. When the current value was seen before, the best candidate partner is exactly that last index, because any older occurrence is even farther away. If the gap is at most k you are done, otherwise overwrite the stored index with the current one and continue.

This is O(n) time and O(n) space. An equivalent view is a sliding window of the last k elements kept in a set: add the new element, check for a repeat, and drop the element that leaves the window. That variant needs only O(min(n, k)) space.
